elements.element: Customer is not subject to any non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 is deleted, and retained Section 12.3 expressly states that Customer has made no non-compete commitment and may develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service.

elements.element: Customer is not subject to any field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so there is no broader or unnamed-product restriction.

elements.element: Any restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains during or after the term; the former 24-month post-term restriction is deleted.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so no restricted period exceeds 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively permits Customer to develop any product or service, which protects internal development.

elements.element: Any restriction includes a carve-out for acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 affirmatively permits Customer to acquire any product or service.

result.reason: The redline deletes only the conflicting non-compete in Section 12.4 and leaves the existing broad freedom-of-operation language in Section 12.3 intact. It fully achieves the preferred position; the fallback limitations are also satisfied because no restriction remains and internal development and acquisitions are expressly permitted.
